item.title: Dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey along the embankment of the Po river in Crescentino
item.description:
Dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey along the embankment of the Po river in Crescentino
Cesare Comina, Andrea Vergnano, Alessandro Arato, Emanuele Duò, Mario Naldi, Dario Chieppa, and Laura Valentina Socco
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8783–8799, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8783-2026, 2026
We present a dataset of a 4 km geophysical survey, executed with a moving system approach, along a river embankment. Data acquisition strategies are discussed and preliminary data analyses are presented. The survey demonstrated the potentiality of the proposed acquisition approach in investigating river embankments. The dataset will be an ideal playground to benchmark alternative interpretation approaches and enable an advancement in the state-of-the-art of these characterization methodologies.

item.title: Towards a global database on building architecture and construction materials for urban climate models
item.description:
Towards a global database on building architecture and construction materials for urban climate models
Lorena de Carvalho Araujo, Valéry Masson, Robert Schoetter, Jean Wurtz, Anouk Le Bihan, and Marion Bonhomme
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8713–8756, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8713-2026, 2026
Urban climate models require information on building materials and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems, which is scarce at the global scale. A survey translated into 11 languages yielded 521 responses from 141 countries. After quality verification and multi-step imputation of missing data, we provide a freely available database of residential building typologies for each country and global non-residential typologies, readily combinable with Local Climate Zone maps.

item.title: A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
item.description:
A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
Ziyue Meng, Yuntao Wang, and Lei Han
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8757–8782, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8757-2026, 2026
A monthly global 3D chlorophyll-a dataset for January 2005–June 2025, covering 10–500 m on a 1° grid, was developed. The dataset was reconstructed using a multimodal deep-learning model that combines Core-Argo temperature and salinity profiles with MODIS surface chlorophyll a and is constrained by BGC-Argo chlorophyll a observations. It provides a new basis for investigating the vertical structure, variability, and long-term changes of ocean chlorophyll a.

item.title: Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
item.description:
Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
Viktor Gouretski, Lijing Cheng, and Juan Du
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8693–8711, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8693-2026, 2026
This study depicts a three-step quality control procedure applied to the Nansen cast temperature profiles (1873–2025, especially before 1970), including automatic/manual quality control and temperature anomaly quality control. Corrections for depth bias are also suggested with improved vertical interpolation procedure. Based on this dataset we access for the first time the change of the ocean heat content of the upper 2000 m layer over a 100 year time period between 1870s and 2020s.

item.title: A multi-year stable isotope dataset of precipitation and groundwater and new hydroisotopic indices for assessing isotopic signal integration in the Sierra de Segura karst aquifer system, southern Spain
item.description:
A multi-year stable isotope dataset of precipitation and groundwater and new hydroisotopic indices for assessing isotopic signal integration in the Sierra de Segura karst aquifer system, southern Spain
Antonio Lope Morales González, Jorge Jódar, Antonio González Ramón, Francisco Moral Martos, Rosario Jiménez Espinosa, and Fernando Gázquez Sánchez
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-779,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We present a six-year record of rainfall and groundwater from a karst water system in southern Spain to understand how rainfall signals are stored and changed underground. We analysed 884 water samples collected between 2017 and 2023. The results show that seasonal changes in rainfall are strongly reduced in groundwater, especially in the deeper aquifer, indicating greater storage and mixing. The dataset provides a valuable reference for studying groundwater recharge and climate variability.

item.title: Improving the freshwater fluxes in global oceanic reanalyses
item.description:
Improving the freshwater fluxes in global oceanic reanalyses
Thomas Vaujour, Louis Kern, Andrea Storto, Julia Pfeffer, Chloé Thenoz, Chunxue Yang, and Stéphanie Guinehut
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-853,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Freshwater fluxes impact the ocean by adding water and changing salinity. To improve the freshwater forcing of ocean models, this study uses artificial intelligence techniques to correct the errors of a hydrological model. The resulting F3O dataset provides a hybrid river discharge estimate with high accuracy, high temporal resolution, and global coverage. It has been implemented in ocean model systems and the results show a significant improvement in the model performance.

item.title: GDDRP-CMIP6: Global Daily Runoff Projections from Bias-Corrected and Downscaled CMIP6 Forcing
item.description:
GDDRP-CMIP6: Global Daily Runoff Projections from Bias-Corrected and Downscaled CMIP6 Forcing
Jiachao Chen, Dai Yamazaki, and Ming Pan
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-862,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
High-resolution, bias-corrected runoff from one globally consistent hydrological framework underpins regional hazard-risk studies and cross-regional comparisons. We developed a global daily runoff at 0.25 degree from 9 CMIP6 models. Compared with the raw runoff, it better reproduces seasonality, mean flow and extremes, and offers a consistent historical baseline while keeping ensemble-mean future trends. It can support flood, drought and water studies worldwide.

item.title: Operational microwave links for hydrometeorological sensing: a multisource dataset for the Czech Republic
item.description:
Operational microwave links for hydrometeorological sensing: a multisource dataset for the Czech Republic
Taoufiq Shit, Martin Fencl, Martin Mudroch, and Vojtěch Bareš
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-939,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Rainfall and moisture in the air are difficult to measure everywhere. We released data from thousands of mobile phone network connections across the Czech Republic, collected over seven months in 2021. Changes in their signals help estimate rain and water vapour. Comparisons with weather stations show promising results, though heavy rain can be underestimated. The openly shared data will help researchers improve weather monitoring using infrastructure that already exists.
